messages.author: ac421cf36d1a4c37
messages.subject: Re: error message
parts:
This is a common factor gwas? do you get this error for just a few snps? have you looked at the individual SNP effects on the factor indicators from the univariate sumstats? are they exactly 0? is there a Z statistic that is exactly 0? you'd need to do a bit of detective work to figure out why there is basically a matrix that is univertable. looking at the additional warnings might also provide clues.
If it's just a few snps out of millions it might be justified to remove them as part of QC loss... hard to say more based on the contents of your email.

messages.author: ac421cf36d1a4c37
messages.subject: Re: error message
parts:
It's still not very clear what your model is and whether it includes individual SNPs or not.
That said, we do not typically recommend changing LDSC intercepts. 
You should be able to tell from documentation what was used to produce the sumstats. I wouldn't move forward with an analysis without knowing where they came from both in terms of participants and GWAS pipeline.
Some of those intercepts are indeed high, although if the mean chisqs are very high, then I suppose this is not as worrisome.
Are some of your phenotypes created by merging (e.g. averaging) other phenotypes? That could create a singular matrix.
